title: the rn self-patch guard
audit_comment: THE RN SELF-PATCH GUARD - the R794 self-patching runner lesson closed structurally (the user Go call on the hardening candidate). A plain re-exec-on-md5-change check still carries the same hole it fixes: bash reads scripts incrementally, and the R794 crash proved the read desyncs BEFORE any mid-script check can run - so the guard goes to the very top: rn always execs a private snapshot copy of itself, the executing read becomes immutable for the run, and the disk rn is free to change mid-run. An engine file patch on rn itself can never desync a landing again; the git add still lands the patched disk copy; a data_files round keeps its one-pass git add because the snapshot is a copy of the CURRENT rn (the R794 DFILES handling rides along). The RN_SNAPSHOT env var is gate and path in one - at most one exec per landing, no loop. splice_engine.py and rverify.py are untouched; the engine double-run and the mixed-state abort stay exactly as they are.

banner.title: THE RN SELF-PATCH GUARD - the snapshot exec, the R794 self-patching runner lesson closed structurally
banner.provenance: The hardening round of the runner (the user Go call, 2026-10-23, on the R795 candidates after the next-arc audit found every book arc closed). R794 proved bash reads a script incrementally: the engine rewrote rn mid-run, the byte offsets shifted, and the landing crashed at line 48 after the all-or-nothing applied 9 - the recovery was the plain re-run, and the lesson said rn can never be a file-patch target of its own run. This round removes the NEVER by making the executing copy immutable: rn execs a private snapshot of itself at the top (one env var, one cp, one exec), removes the snapshot on every exit path (the trap), and otherwise changes nothing. Registry 478 live, unchanged; the battery census reads loaded 478, errors 0.

file_patches.note: the snapshot-exec guard after set - eu (the R794 self-patching runner lesson closed structurally)
file_patches.to:
set -eu

# ---- the self-patch guard (the R794 lesson): bash reads
# ---- scripts incrementally, so an engine file patch on rn
# ---- itself desyncs the executing read - run from a private
# ---- snapshot copy instead; the disk rn is free to change
# ---- mid-run, and the git add still lands the patched copy
if [ -z "${RN_SNAPSHOT:-}" ]; then
    RN_SNAPSHOT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rn.self.$$"
    export RN_SNAPSHOT
    cp "$0" "$RN_SNAPSHOT"
    exec bash "$RN_SNAPSHOT" "$@"
fi
trap 'rm -f "$RN_SNAPSHOT"' EXIT
